messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

The user gave a "raw" input representation containing a long list of reports (events) with revisions and a future schedule. We need to follow the instructions.

Goal: Simulate a lost-sales inventory system: Received receipts add quantity to stock. Demand events consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet portion is lost (lost sales). A "stockout" means there was unmet demand strictly positive; not just ending at zero.

We are given initial_stock = 17. Target_time = 100, horizon_time = 130.

We have knowledge_cutoff = 100, which is the time up to which we see reports (received_time). We must filter reports: keep only those with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then for each event_id, choose the highest visible revision (i.e., highest revision number among those kept). Revisions replace earlier reports: only one final event per event_id (the latest revision visible before cutoff). Then we keep events that have event_time <= target_time (100) (i.e., only those after revision selection). Then we order the chosen events by (event_time, event_id) order (i.e., sort ascending by event_time, then perhaps lexical order of event_id as tie-breaker). Then we apply these events in order from initial_stock. This yields historical stock at target_time (i.e., after processing all events up to time <= target_time). Also we need to track total historical_lost: sum of unmet demand across all demand events (visible ones) up to target_time. For those events that have event_time <= target_time (i.e., up to 100). Also we must compute stock_at_target: the stock after processing up to target_time.

After that, the scenario: apply future_schedule events (the known hypothetical future scenario) (which have times between 102 and 130). The future schedule events are given; we apply them after reconstructing historical stock at time target_time, starting from stock_at_target at time target_time (i.e., after the historical events up to 100). The future schedule events are applied in order of (event_time, event_id). There should be no overlapping times (mostly each different time). We need to compute final stock after horizon_time (130) after processing all future events. Also we need to compute future_lost: sum of unmet demands from future events ONLY (not including any already lost historically). Also we need first_future_stockout_time: earliest event_time among future events where there was some unmet demand (stockout) i.e., demand > stock, so stockout time is that event_time; if no future demand unmet, output -1.

Important: Stockout is defined as strictly positive unmet demand, not just ending with zero stock after demand. So if the demand exactly matches stock, stock goes to zero and no stockout occurs. Only if demand > stock.

We need to produce five integers: stock_at_target, historical_lost, stock_at_horizon, future_lost, first_future_stockout_time.

Now we need to process the reports.
